title: Series 63 low water cut-off: burner does not shut off on low water
equipment: McDonnell & Miller Series 63 low water cut-off

n1.text: Safety first: the boiler may be running dry. Ask the tech to confirm the water level in the gauge glass. Is the water level actually below the control?

options.label: Yes, level is low and the burner is still on

r_ok.cause: The control is not being asked to shut off; this is not a cut-off failure.
fix: Have the tech confirm the actual water level before testing further.
Blow down the control per the maintenance procedure and confirm the burner shuts off when the level falls.

n2.text: With the water level below the control, ask the tech (power isolated per lockout/tagout) to check whether terminals C and N.C. are open. Are they open?

r_mud.cause: The float chamber is probably loaded with mud or sediment, or the contacts are fused together.
fix: Have the tech open and clean the float chamber and check for scale or sediment between the bellows corrugations.
Remove the switch and operate it manually; if C and N.C. will not open or contacts are fused, replace the switch.
Check the electrical load is within the switch ratings.

r_other.cause: The control is cutting out correctly, so the problem is downstream in the burner circuit.
fix: Escalate to the boiler/controls contractor to trace the burner safety circuit wiring.
Do not bypass the low water cut-off.
